narrative.overview: Ledgerly feels like a well-kept financial notebook translated into a precise digital tool. It is light, legible, and calm under sustained use. Dense information is organized through alignment, typography, and tonal surfaces instead of decorative containers. The system is product-first. Familiar controls and restrained motion let the interface disappear behind review, filtering, and analysis.
keyCharacteristics: Quiet, cool-neutral surfaces with one authoritative emerald action color.
Compact but readable typography with tabular financial figures.
Visible uncertainty, duplicate status, privacy boundaries, and next actions.
Structural responsive behavior rather than shrinking type or hiding core controls.
State-driven motion only, with reduced-motion support.

rules.name: The One Authority Rule
rules.body: Emerald is reserved for actions, focus, selection, and confirmed state. If it appears as decoration, remove it.

rules.name: The Explicit State Rule
rules.body: Success, warning, error, debit, and credit always include words or icons. Color never carries the meaning alone.

rules.name: The Accounting Line Rule
rules.body: Columns of currency, confidence, dates, and balances use tabular numerals and align by value, not by decoration.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If removing a shadow does not reduce comprehension, the shadow is forbidden.

dos: Do keep financial values explicit with currency codes or symbols, signs, and tabular numerals.
Do keep body and placeholder text at WCAG 2.2 AA contrast or higher.
Do distinguish empty accounts from empty filtered results and provide the next useful action.
Do use 150-220ms state transitions and remove non-essential motion for reduced-motion users.
Do make tenant isolation and aggregate-only AI behavior inspectable in copy and documentation.
donts: Don't use trading-terminal cosplay with black surfaces, neon ticks, and artificial urgency.
Don't build generic AI-finance dashboards from interchangeable metric cards, gradients, and vague claims.
Don't use gamified budgeting, confetti, shame, or red-versus-green color as the only signal.
Don't use decorative glassmorphism, oversized radii, gradient text, or colored side-stripe borders.
Don't pair 1px borders with wide decorative shadows on cards or buttons.
Don't combine unrelated currencies into one total or chart.
Don't make security claims that are not backed by visible architecture, tests, or precise behavior.
